AgentloopRef.description:
The admitted Agentloop a session runs: which one, how it is configured, which
Environment of the session runs it.

url.description: HTTPS URL fetched by the model provider.

format.description: Versioned adapter format; incompatible adapters must reject the item.

is_error.description:
ALWAYS set on a failed tool. Omitting the flag on a failure lets the
model read that failure as a success.

media.description: Model-visible media alongside the ordinary JSON Tool output.

environments.description:
The Environments of this session, set up as part of this create. Every Tool and
the Agentloop name one of them.

idle_ttl_ms.description:
How long the session may sit idle before Brain suspends it: its task and memory
are released and rebuilt from disk on the next request. Absent means the server's
default; zero means never.

response_format.description:
The provider's structured-output request, applied to every model call unless the
loop sends its own. Optional, and rejected at create for a provider that cannot
carry it.

system.description:
The system prompt the agent loop starts from. The loop may send a different one
on any model call.

transcript.description:
A transcript to carry forward, if the caller has one: the messages the new
session's first model call should already see. Brain journals them as the session's
opening transcript. Empty is an ordinary new session.

Environment.description:
One Environment a session declares: a name unique within the session, how Brain
reaches it, and its own configuration, which Brain carries and never reads.

oneOf.description: Managed by brain-server in its native Environment worker pool.

The process that registered as this host, reached over the connection it holds
open: a browser tab, a Node process, a server.

Reached over HTTP. `credential` is sent as a bearer token; the server seals it
beside the model key and never journals it.

lifecycle.description: Required on new admissions; absence only supports retained session journals.

EnvironmentControlRequest.description: The same service request in every extension role and transport.

EnvironmentGrant.description: Authority over a declared binding and instances made from its template.

EnvironmentOperation.description: One operation on an Environment, named by `(session_id, environment, sequence)`.

context.description: Controller services are separate from the hosted invocation's callback.

sequence.description:
The sequence of the journal record that started this operation. With
`session_id` it names the operation: a redelivery carries the same pair, so a
receiver that already answered it can say so.

on_turn_end.description: Setup may register a method Brain calls after each turn, with its start sequence.

oneOf.description: The entrypoint returned; only an explicit finish closes a Tool execution.

callback.description: Sent only during execution, never journaled.

implementation.description: Interpreted only by the Environment; fixes the runtime entrypoint and configuration.

EnvironmentTemplate.description: Fixed at admission. Provider configuration is validated, never interpreted by Brain.

Event.description:
One journal record as a client reads it. `(session_id, sequence)` names it; there
is no other identifier.

origin.description: Absent on kernel records and historical extension records without attribution.

ExecutionCallback.description: Where a remote invocation reaches only its caller-granted services.

sequence.description: The command this Event belongs to.
The sequence Brain assigned to the committed Event.

HostOperation.description:
What a host is asked to do for a session placed in it. A call is named by the
command's `(session_id, sequence)`; the Tool's own call id never leaves Brain.

options.description: Presentation options validated by the selected adapter; never execution authority.

response_format.description: Absent inherits the session default; null resets it; an object sets it.

system.description:
The system prompt for this call. Absent means the one the session was created
with; empty means none. The session fills it in before the call is journalled.

tools.description:
The tools to offer on this call, by name. Absent means every tool the session was
created with; each name given must be one of them. Filled in like `system`.

Outcome.description:
The one envelope every tool invocation resolves to.

`timeout` is distinguished from `error` because the deadline is caller-owned: no
backend family can be trusted to enforce one remotely, so the caller kills and says
exactly what happened rather than encoding it as an exit code.

SessionSummary.description: What the API says about a session: its id, where it is, and how far its journal goes.

last_sequence.description:
Sequence of the last journal record committed for this session — the journal is
complete through here, so it is where a `GET /events` cursor starts.

SessionTranscript.description: Canonical transcript as of a committed journal sequence, available without execution.

oneOf.description:
The provider ended the stream without a terminal reason. Distinct from
EndTurn on purpose: absent is never zero.

Tool.description:
A canonical Tool definition with one implementation per authorized Environment.
Brain validates dispatched inputs and successful outputs against this definition.

placements.description: One implementation per authorized Environment, fixed at create.

ToolDefinition.description: What the model may be told about a Tool.

ToolOutput.description: A Tool observation with an optional presentation for the Agentloop.

content.description: Optional model-facing text; the structured output and failure status are unchanged.

ToolReturn.description: Observations available when the synchronous phase returns. Execution can remain open.

TurnError.description: Why a turn, or one of the host calls inside it, failed.

Usage.description:
Provider-reported usage. Every field is `Option` because **absent is never
zero** -- a provider that does not report cache reads is not a provider that
read zero cache tokens.

total_input_tokens.description: Inclusive input, including cache reads and writes. Raw input remains dialect-specific.

UserInput.description: What an application hands a session on `send`.
